author: Eric Berne
provenance: Structured reference material (paraphrased, no verbatim reproduction).

slices.summary: Definition of the three ego states (Parent, Adult, Child) and their observable markers; Critical vs Nurturing Parent; Natural / Adapted / Little Professor variants of Child; contamination and exclusion as two failure modes.
slices.usageNote: Core teaching material for this chapter. Paraphrase only; do not quote.

slices.summary: 1964 examples in the original book are gendered and dated; modern ChapterFlow scenarios must be drawn from neutral contemporary settings. The observational content of the model is preserved; the case studies are replaced.
slices.usageNote: Global framing constraint for Ch1 examples and moral-complexity handling.

slices.summary: Chapter 1 intent: introduce Parent / Adult / Child as behavioral states, focus on the observational skill, reserve transactions / games / strokes / payoffs for Chs 2–4.
slices.usageNote: Scope guard. Do not anticipate later chapters.

slices.summary: State-shifts are mostly unchosen. A person slipping from Adult into Parent is not making a decision; the shift happens without their permission. The model gives the person a way to notice after the fact.
slices.usageNote: Load-bearing for the chapter's hard-depth tension: observational vs executive.

slices.summary: The three qualities of autonomy (awareness, spontaneity, intimacy) are the destination of the whole book. Awareness is a long arc of Ch1's observational skill but that language belongs to Ch10.
slices.usageNote: Forbidden-drift marker. Do not reference 'awareness' as a term in Ch1.

forbiddenContent: Verbatim or near-verbatim reproduction of Berne's prose.
Reproduction of Berne's original gendered case studies.
References to Freud by name beyond one paraphrase ('not those three').
Any extension into transactions, games, strokes, payoffs, or life positions (later chapters).
Any neurochemistry, hormones, evolutionary psychology, or millisecond claims.
